messages.content: Make one narrow 8-second beat-grouping decision. Return JSON only.

LEFT:
A technician unlocks a storage cabinet, removes a heavy equipment case, carries it across the room, and sets it on a bench.

RIGHT:
The technician opens the case, removes the calibration unit, connects it to the machine, and starts a full diagnostic cycle.

Can every concrete visible action/state in LEFT and RIGHT fit naturally in one 8-second video beat?
MERGE only for one immediate continuous action chain or natural setup/completion chain.
KEEP_SEPARATE if they are distinct tasks/phases, if LEFT is a calm baseline before a new danger/change, if combining would compress required actions, or if RIGHT is explicitly long/repeated.
Return exactly {"decision":"MERGE|KEEP_SEPARATE"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to decide whether all concrete visible action/state in LEFT and RIGHT can fit naturally in one 8-second video beat. We have two sequences:

LEFT: technician unlocks a storage cabinet, removes heavy equipment case, carries it across the room, sets on bench.

RIGHT: technician opens case, removes calibration unit, connects it to machine, starts full diagnostic cycle.

We need to see if all actions can fit in 8 seconds. Let's estimate durations: unlocking cabinet maybe 1 sec; removing case from cabinet maybe 0.5-1 sec; carrying across room maybe 2 secs; setting on bench maybe 1 sec. So left ~4-5 secs. Right: opening case maybe 0.5 sec; removing calibration unit maybe 1 sec; connecting to machine maybe 1 sec; starting diagnostic cycle maybe 0.5 sec? But "full diagnostic cycle" might be longer, but the action of starting it is just a button press. So right ~3-4 secs. Combined could be about 7-9 secs. If we merge them into one beat, would all actions fit naturally? The left tasks are before the right: after setting on bench, technician opens case and removes calibration unit etc. That seems natural sequence. But can it compress to 8 seconds? Possibly yes if each action is quick.

But "full diagnostic cycle" might be a longer process but starting it could be just pressing start; the rest of cycle may take time beyond beat. The question: "Can every concrete visible action/state in LEFT and RIGHT fit naturally in one 8-second video beat?" If full diagnostic cycle takes more than 8 seconds, then maybe not.

But they say "RIGHT is explicitly long/repeated." They mention if RIGHT is explicitly long/repeated. In this case, the diagnostic cycle might be longer; but it's a single action of starting it? The phrase "full diagnostic cycle" could imply that the machine runs for some time. But visible action: starts full diagnostic cycle (press start). That is one action.

Thus all actions can fit in 8 seconds if each is quick. So MERGE likely.

But check: left has heavy equipment case removal and carrying across room; right has opening case, removing calibration unit, connecting to machine, starting diagnostic cycle. These are distinct tasks but sequential. They could be merged into one beat of 8 secs? The bench setting might take some time before the technician can open it. But it's okay.

Thus decision: MERGE.
